A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Data-Juicer Sandbox work. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization and added experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original MGM-2B and EasyAnimate operator-selection, combination, and data-repetition experiments, plus T2V-Turbo modifications and ablations in Appendix B.3.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds CLIP experiments, a full-fine-tuning MGM comparison, word-entropy analysis, and video self-evolution results.

M1.justification: The sandbox workflow and existing LoRA initialization, self-distillation, and real-data loss remain. Appendix E.7 adds a further video self-evolution stage using the earlier Data-Juicer model as teacher, additional aesthetics/motion filtering, and reduced reward weights. This extends the existing video-training procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds DataComp-based CLIP image-text pre-training to the retained image-to-text and text-to-video tasks. Its evaluation covers 40 benchmark measurements spanning classification, image-text retrieval, and fairness-related scenarios, including ImageNet derivatives, MSCOCO, Dollar Street, and GeoDE (Appendices D.2 and D.6).

E2.justification: The reported VBench comparator set changes substantially. v2 Tables 3/11 add Gen-3, Kling, CogVideoX-5B, and Vchitect 2.0-2B; Gen-2, VideoCrafter-2.0, Pika Beta, and AnimateDiff-V2 from v1 Table 2 are no longer tabulated there. T2V-Turbo, VEnhancer, and LaVie-2 remain in the comparison.

E3.justification: v2 introduces CLIP experiments varying ViT-B-32/ViT-B-16 and compute scale, plus a MGM comparison using full fine-tuning data after four repetitions of selected pretraining data. Appendix E.7 adds a video stage reported as four epochs. Its budget conflicts with the main text and cost tables, but the substantial addition of experimental protocols is clear.

E4.justification: v2 adds CLIP recipe analyses across compute scales and encoder configurations, a quantitative word-entropy check of data diversity (Table 8), and a self-evolution extension to the cumulative video ablation (Table 10). Appendix C.2 also reports exploratory bucket-count trials. The original correlation and cluster-recipe analyses are retained under new numbering.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 3(a,c) reports standard deviations for top-operator recipes; corresponding v2 Figure 2(a,b) removes them without restoring those recipe uncertainties elsewhere. Single-operator and cluster-recipe deviations remain in Table 6 and Figure 9. Detailed MGM three-run and EasyAnimate two-run protocols are retained; new CLIP results lack a run-count disclosure.

E6.justification: The original operator-ranking table and correlation matrices are numerically unchanged. v2 adds CLIP results, a MGM comparison reporting +2.12% average performance change (Table 9), and a video self-evolution result of 82.53 total, 83.38 quality, and 79.13 semantic score (Table 10). The earlier 82.10/83.14/77.93 result remains; the new result uses additional training and data.

T1.justification: v1 defines operator and pyramid data pools but provides no corresponding cost/error analysis. v2 Section 3.2.4 and Appendix C introduce a formal training-cost comparison and a Hoeffding-based derivation relating small-pool and full-data performance changes, with new boundedness and expected-effect assumptions.

C1.justification: The claimed scope expands from multimodal generative-model co-development to include non-generative CLIP representation learning, explicitly incorporated into the abstract and contributions. v2 also claims consistent CLIP compute-scaling behavior. The original open-source sandbox and Probe-Analyze-Refine contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation of CLIP-based filtering as implicit distillation, an assumption that caption entropy represents visual diversity, and substantive discussion of cost versus feedback informativeness. It also identifies limits concerning larger CLIP models, untested non-filter operators, and unavailable information for some cost comparisons.

D1.justification: v2 adds a sandbox launch command and dependency/lazy-loading guidance, CLIP data-recovery and pool-size details, named reward models and explicit loss coefficients, and runtime/FLOPs estimation procedures. Existing MGM/EasyAnimate implementation details and the code/data/model access link are largely retained. These are substantial additional disclosures, not evidence that every underlying implementation changed.

R1.justification: The model-centric, data-centric, and infrastructure positioning remains, largely relocated to Appendix A. v2 adds focused contrasts with DataComp and MetaCLIP, alongside references for CLIP scaling, Data-Juicer 2.0, and new video and reward models. This extends the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: The title changes from Comprehensive to Feedback-Driven, and substantial prose is rewritten or condensed. Experimental applications and results are merged into Section 4, infrastructure and detailed related work move into appendices, and the appendix gains an extensive roadmap. Impact and reproducibility statements are also added.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout. The architecture diagram is redrawn and relocated; recipe diagrams are split between main text and appendix, with CLIP panels added to recipe and scaling figures. New scenario, MGM, CLIP, diversity, and cost tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The CLIP scaling experiments and full-fine-tuning MGM comparison strengthen empirical support for recipe transfer, while entropy analysis tests a previously qualitative diversity explanation. The net gain is limited by conflicting video-training budgets in Appendix E.7 and Tables 3/12, removed recipe uncertainty values, and Appendix C's claim of exponential dependence on sampling ratio without deriving that dependence.
